summary: SKYBLINK blinkoscope is a web-based astronomical laboratory designed to explore multi-epoch infrared observations from NASA's SPHEREx mission, historical WISE data, and ESA Gaia DR3 astrometric sources. The platform features interactive multi-epoch comparison modes—including time-lapse blinking, ping-pong bounce, epoch subtraction, and deep co-add stacking—to help users visually isolate transient, variable, or moving celestial objects. Built with a Python FastAPI backend, it handles FITS file streaming, WCS coordinate parsing, background and zodiacal subtraction, peak detection, and candidate tracking, while offering a responsive dark-mode frontend equipped with Chart.js aperture photometry, spectra generation, and multi-format data export options.
details: SKYBLINK blinkoscope is an advanced web-based astronomical laboratory designed to process and analyze multi-epoch infrared observations from NASA's SPHEREx mission and archival WISE data. Developed to tackle the challenges of cosmic motion and transient discovery, the platform features interactive time-lapse blinking, ping-pong bounce comparison, epoch subtraction ($T_2 - T_1$), and deep co-add stacking, enabling users to effortlessly isolate variable stars, moving objects, and distant celestial bodies. Powered by a robust Python FastAPI backend, SKYBLINK handles FITS streaming, WCS coordinate parsing, zodiacal background subtraction, and automated candidate tracking. This is paired with a high-performance dark-mode frontend equipped with Chart.js aperture photometry, spectral generation, and ESA Gaia DR3 proper-motion overlays. Crucially, the platform includes built-in resilience against archive gateway interruptions to ensure uninterrupted analysis. This tool is vital because it transforms complex, heavy astronomical datasets into an intuitive, accessible, and interactive experience for both professional researchers and citizen scientists.
